info.title: NeonPanel API
info.summary: Public REST API for NeonPanel: companies, inventory, documents, reports and imports. Currently in beta.
info.description:
> **This API is in beta.**
> It is stable enough to build against, but it is not frozen. Fields may be added, endpoints may
> change shape, and behaviour described here may still be corrected as it is verified against the
> implementation. Ignore response fields you do not recognise rather than validating strictly
> against these schemas, and re-read this page after every version bump.

The NeonPanel API exposes the data behind [my.neonpanel.com](https://my.neonpanel.com):
company context, the inventory catalogue, accounting documents
(inventory orders, bills, shipments, invoices, assembly orders, adjustments),
reports and analytics, and document import.

## Base URL

All endpoints are served from a single origin:

```
https://my.neonpanel.com
```

Business endpoints live under the `/api/v1` prefix. OAuth 2.0 endpoints live under
`/oauth2` and are **not** versioned.

## Authentication

Every endpoint requires an OAuth 2.0 bearer access token unless it is explicitly
documented as public. Pass the token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

The API uses the **Authorization Code flow with PKCE (S256)**. The `openid` scope is
required; no other scopes are currently defined.

| Step | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Register a client (optional, open DCR) | `POST /oauth2/register` |
| 2. Send the user to authorize | `GET /oauth2/authorize` |
| 3. Exchange the code for tokens | `POST /oauth2/token` |
| 4. Refresh an expired token | `POST /oauth2/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` |

Public endpoints — the ones that do **not** take a bearer access token — are
`GET /oauth2/authorize` and `POST /oauth2/register`. The token endpoint authenticates
the *client*, not the user, and accepts `none`, `client_secret_basic`,
`client_secret_post` or `private_key_jwt`. The client-management endpoints under
`/oauth2/register/{client_id}` authenticate with a **Registration Access Token (RAT)**,
which is a different credential from an API access token and is valid for 30 days.

## Company scope

Most business endpoints are scoped to a company via the `{companyUuid}` path
parameter. Access is validated server-side against the token's user; a company the
user cannot access returns `403`. Use `GET /api/v1/companies` to list the companies
available to the current token.

## Entry Locked Date

Each company has an **Entry Locked Date** that closes its accounting history. A document dated
earlier than that date cannot be created, changed or deleted, and any such request is rejected
with `400`. The date moves forward as periods are closed, so an endpoint that worked yesterday can
start rejecting the same payload today.

## Pagination

Paginated endpoints return `current_page`, `per_page` and `last_page` at the top level of the
response, next to `data` — not nested under a `pagination` key. They accept `page` and `per_page`
query parameters, and default page sizes differ per resource.

Not every list is paginated. Sales channels, payment terms and reports come back as a plain `data`
array with no page fields at all.

## Errors

Errors return a JSON body with a `message` field. Validation failures return `422`
with a field-keyed `errors` object.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | Malformed request |
| `401` | Missing, expired or invalid access token |
| `403` | Authenticated, but not permitted for this company or resource |
| `404` | Resource does not exist or is outside the company scope |
| `422` | Validation failed |

get.description:
Returns the companies the authenticated user can access, paginated.

Two identifiers come back for each company and they are not interchangeable: `uuid` is what every company-scoped endpoint expects as its `{companyUuid}` path parameter, while the numeric `id` is what report URLs expect as the `company` query parameter.
Returns every permission defined in the platform, independent of what the authenticated user actually holds. Use the returned keys as the `{permission}` path parameter elsewhere.
Returns the companies in which the authenticated user holds the given permission. Look up valid permission keys with `GET /api/v1/permissions`.

parameters.name: permission
parameters.description: Name of Permission which the User must have in Companies

parameters.name: company_uuids
parameters.description: Filter by Companies. Defaults to all accessible for user companies

get.description: Returns the permissions the authenticated user holds in the given company. Use this to decide which operations to offer before calling them, rather than relying on `403` responses.

Returns the reports the authenticated user can open, each with its group, description and direct `link`. The `link` alone opens the report with its default sheet; call `GET /api/v1/reports/{reportId}` first to discover which sheets and query parameters it accepts.

Returns basic report info and a list of sheets with supported parameters. Build report URL by appending query parameters to `link`: {link}?sheet={sheets[].slug}&{parameter.slug}={value}&... The `sheet` query parameter is optional. If `sheet` is not provided, the report will open the first available sheet by default. You can additionally pass the `company` query parameter as a comma-separated list of company IDs. Each value is the numeric `id` returned by `GET /api/v1/companies` — not `uuid` and not `short_name`. The order of query parameters does not matter. Example: {link}?company=106,296&sheet=transaction-list&start-date=2026-01-01

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: Report ID obtained in listReports operation

get.description:
Returns revenue and cost of goods sold aggregated over a date range.

`periodicity` controls how the range is bucketed (`total`, `yearly`, `quarterly` or `monthly`) and `grouping` controls the dimension results are broken down by, defaulting to company. Both `company_uuids` and `country_codes` narrow the scope; left out, they cover everything the authenticated user can access. `end_date` defaults to today.

parameters.name: company_uuids
parameters.description: Filter by Companies. Defaults to all accessible for user companies

parameters.name: country_codes
parameters.description: Filter by countries. Defaults to all accessible for company marketplaces

parameters.name: grouping
parameters.description: Type of grouping of results. If not provided, company grouping will be set

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Defaults to current date if not provided

200.description: Sales and COGS summary data retrieved successfully

get.description: Returns the company's warehouses, paginated. Supports free-text search by name.

Returns what a single warehouse currently holds, paginated — one entry per inventory item. For the opposite view — one item across every warehouse — use `GET /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/inventory-items/{inventoryId}/balances`.

parameters.name: balances_date
parameters.description: Set a date if you need a balances in a past. Defaults to current date if not provided

get.description: Returns the company's inventory items, paginated. Supports free-text search and filtering through query parameters.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search by SKU, ASIN, FnSKU, ID or Name

200.description: List of inventory items retrieved successfully

post.description: Creates an inventory item in the company. Returns the created item with its manager, product and listing relations resolved.

get.description: Returns a single inventory item with its manager, product and listing relations resolved.

parameters.name: inventoryId
parameters.description: The ID of the inventory item

put.description: Updates an inventory item. Returns the updated item with its manager, product and listing relations resolved.

parameters.name: inventoryId
parameters.description: The ID of the inventory item

parameters.name: inventoryId
parameters.description: The ID of the inventory item

get.summary: Get Inventory Item Balances and Restock Data
get.description: Returns a single inventory item together with its restock recommendation and a per-warehouse breakdown of current balances. For the opposite view — everything held in one warehouse — use `GET /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/warehouses/{warehouseUuid}/balances`.

parameters.name: inventoryId
parameters.description: The ID of the inventory item

parameters.name: balances_date
parameters.description: Set a date if you need a balances information in a past. Defaults to current date if not provided

get.description: Returns the landed cost records for an inventory item — the manufacturing and delivery expenses that make up its cost basis — broken down by period and warehouse.

parameters.name: inventoryId
parameters.description: The ID of the inventory item

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Defaults to current date if not provided

get.description: Returns the cost of goods sold recorded against an inventory item, broken down by period, together with the documents each figure was derived from.

parameters.name: inventoryId
parameters.description: The ID of the inventory item

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Defaults to current date if not provided

get.description: Returns the company's products, paginated and filterable through query parameters. A product groups one or more inventory items.

id.description: ID of Product. It will return only 1 product if such was found

search.description: Search by SKU, Name or Parent SKU

post.description: Creates a product in the company and returns it.

put.description: Updates a product and returns it.

200.description: Product data updated and retrieved successfully

delete.description: Deletes a product. Inventory items previously grouped by it are not deleted.

get.description: Returns the company's listings, paginated and filterable through query parameters. A listing is the link between an inventory item and the offer that sells it on a marketplace.

id.description: ID of Product. It will return only 1 product if such was found

post.description: Fetches the listing from Amazon, updates the stored record and returns it. Use this when marketplace data has changed and waiting for the scheduled sync is not acceptable.

200.description: Listings data updated and retrieved successfully

get.description: Returns the field structure expected by the JSON import endpoint for the given document type, including a description of each field. Fetch this first, then build the payload for `POST /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/create/{type}`.

200.description: Instructions by specified type found and provided

attributes.description: Object with keys as parameter name and value as description

post.description: Creates documents from a JSON payload. Get the expected structure for the document type from `GET /api/v1/import/{type}/instructions` before calling this.

data.description: Document parameters with line items included. Get the expected structure from `GET /api/v1/import/{type}/instructions`.

X-Request-Id.description: Echo of the generated request ID.

documents.description: Documents created from the uploaded file.

400.description: Unsupported type or data is broken.

get.description: Returns the company-wide defaults used by inventory forecasting: supplier and Amazon FBA lead times, safety stock coverage, replenishment and planned PO frequencies, and the Pareto and revenue class thresholds. These apply wherever an inventory item does not carry its own value.

default_seasonality.description: 12 multipliers for each month in a year separated by semicolon

default_lead_time_days.description: Default supplier lead time in days

default_safety_stock_days.description: Default safety stock coverage in days

default_fba_lead_time.description: Default Amazon FBA lead time in days

default_fba_safety_stock.description: Default FBA safety stock coverage in days

put.description: Updates the company-wide forecasting defaults. Send only the settings being changed. The response confirms the save with a `success` flag and does not echo the stored values — read them back with `GET` if you need to confirm.

default_seasonality.description: 12 multipliers for each month in a year separated by semicolon

default_lead_time_days.description: Default supplier lead time in days

default_safety_stock_days.description: Default safety stock coverage in days

default_fba_lead_time.description: Default Amazon FBA lead time in days

default_fba_safety_stock.description: Default FBA safety stock coverage in days

success.description: Indication that parameters have been saved successfully

post.description:
Creates documents by extracting them from a PDF.

Send the file as a raw `application/pdf` body with the `filename` query parameter set. If streaming the file is not possible, send JSON instead with a `file` object holding a short-lived download link.

Processing is asynchronous. A `202` response carries a `requestId` and a `Retry-After` header — wait that many seconds, or 15 if the header is missing, then poll `GET /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/import/{type}/status/{requestId}`.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Original filename to store alongside the uploaded PDF, required for application/pdf request

link.description: Short-lived URL to GET the file.

202.description: Accepted for processing. First status check should occur after 15 seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the first status poll.

400.description: Unsupported type or file is broken.

get.description:
Returns the outcome of a PDF import, identified by the `requestId` from the upload response.

While processing is still running the endpoint responds `202 Accepted` with a `Retry-After` header. Wait that many seconds, or 5 if the header is missing, then poll again.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: Request ID of the previously created import.

X-Request-Id.description: Echo of the generated request ID.

documents.description: Documents created from the uploaded file.

202.description: Not ready yet. Client should poll again after the suggested delay.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before next poll (default 5).

X-Request-Id.description: Echo of the generated request ID.

get.description: Returns the company's inventory orders, paginated. Each order arrives with its line items, warehouse, marketplace, vendor and payment requests. Optional server-side filters are passed as query parameters under the `filters` key.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search string applied across order fields.

parameters.name: warehouses
parameters.description: Filter by one or more warehouse IDs.

parameters.name: vendors
parameters.description: Filter by one or more vendor IDs.

post.description:
Creates an inventory order. The authenticated user is recorded as its creator.

If `payment_term_id` is set, payment request installments are generated automatically from the term's schema. Adjust them afterwards one at a time with `PUT /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/payment-requests/{paymentId}`.

Returns `400` if `date_products_manufactured` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description: Returns a single inventory order with every relation resolved: line items with product info, warehouse, marketplace, vendor and payment requests. Responds `404` if the order does not belong to the company in `companyUuid`.

put.description:
Updates an inventory order. Only fields present in the request body are applied; omitted fields keep their current values.

Sending `details` replaces the line items entirely — the existing ones are deleted and re-created — so send the complete set, not only the lines that changed.

Sending `payment_term_id` re-syncs the payment request schedule against the term rather than rebuilding it. Installments the new term still needs are left untouched, including any edits made to them; only the ones it no longer needs are deleted. Sending the term the document already has changes nothing. To change a single installment's `paid_amount`, `payment_date`, `transaction_number` or `memo`, use `PUT /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/payment-requests/{paymentId}` instead.

Returns `400` if `date_products_manufactured` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description: Returns the company's bills, paginated. Each bill arrives with its line items (including service and service group), vendor and payment requests. Optional server-side filters are passed as query parameters.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search string applied across bill fields.

parameters.name: vendors
parameters.description: Filter by one or more vendor IDs.

post.description:
Creates a bill. The authenticated user is recorded as its creator.

Every line item in `details` needs a `service_id` — look the options up with `GET /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/services`. The optional `documents` array links the bill back to the documents it was raised for; supported types are `InventoryOrder`, `AssemblyOrder`, `Shipment` and `Invoice`.

If `payment_term_id` is set, payment request installments are generated automatically from the term's schema. Adjust them afterwards one at a time with `PUT /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/payment-requests/{paymentId}`.

Returns `400` if `date` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description: Returns a single bill with every relation resolved: line items with service and service group, vendor and payment requests. Responds `404` if the bill does not belong to the company in `companyUuid`.

put.description:
Updates a bill. Only fields present in the request body are applied; omitted fields keep their current values.

Sending `details` replaces the line items entirely — the existing ones are deleted and re-created — so send the complete set, not only the lines that changed. Every line item needs a `service_id` — look the options up with `GET /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/services`.

`documents` behaves differently: entries are synced by upsert, so new ones are created, matching ones are updated and ones no longer in the array are removed. All entries must share the same `type`; entries of any other type are dropped without an error, so mixing types silently loses data.

Sending `payment_term_id` re-syncs the payment request schedule against the term rather than rebuilding it. Installments the new term still needs are left untouched, including any edits made to them; only the ones it no longer needs are deleted. Sending the term the document already has changes nothing. To change a single installment, use `PUT /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/payment-requests/{paymentId}` instead.

Returns `400` if `date` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description: Returns the company's payment request installments across every document type, paginated. Each entry is a flat merge of the installment's own fields and a nested `document` object describing the parent document it was generated from. Supports date range filtering by `due_date`. The default page size is 20.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Filter payment requests with `due_date` >= this date (ISO 8601).

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Filter payment requests with `due_date` <= this date (ISO 8601).

200.description: Paginated list of payment requests with document context.

put.description:
Updates a single payment request installment. Only fields present in the request body are applied; omitted fields keep their current values. Returns the installment merged with its parent document context — the same shape as the entries in the list endpoint.

This is the only way to change an individual installment. Edits made here survive a later `payment_term_id` sync on the parent document, as long as the new term still calls for that installment.

200.description: The updated payment request with document context.

get.description: Returns the company's vendors, paginated. Supports free-text search by name. The default page size is 100; override it with `per_page`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search applied against vendor name.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of results per page. Defaults to 100.

get.description: Returns the company's assembly orders, paginated. Each order arrives with its line items (including assembly and product info), warehouse and marketplace. Supports free-text search and date range filtering by `assembled_at`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search applied across assembly order fields.

parameters.name: warehouses
parameters.description: Filter by one or more warehouse IDs.

post.description:
Creates an assembly order. `ref_number` is the only required field. Every other field is optional and nullable, and can be sent here or added later with `PUT`. A project task is created for the document on save, or reused if one already exists.

Returns `400` if `date_order_assembled` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description: Returns a single assembly order with every relation resolved: line items with assembly and product info, warehouse, marketplace and the linked project task. Responds `404` if the order does not belong to the company in `companyUuid`.

put.description:
Updates an assembly order. Only fields present in the request body are applied; omitted fields keep their current values. `ref_number` is fixed at creation and cannot be changed — it is ignored if present in the request body. Every other field can be updated.

Sending `items` replaces the line items entirely — the existing ones are deleted and re-created — so send the complete set, not only the lines that changed.

Returns `400` if `date_order_assembled` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date. Both the incoming date and the order's current date are checked, so an order already sitting before the locked date cannot be moved forward out of it.

get.description:
Returns the company's invoices, paginated. Each invoice arrives with its line items, customer, warehouse, sales channel, `source` and `market` — the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the marketplace the sale belongs to.

Supports free-text search across invoice fields, and date range filtering by `transaction_date` through `start_date` and `end_date`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search applied across invoice fields.

post.description:
Creates a manual invoice. `ref_number` is the only required field. Every other field is optional and nullable, and can be sent here or added later with `PUT`. A project task is created for the document on save, or reused if one already exists.

Each line item in `details` requires a `service_id`, even when the line sells stock — look the options up with `GET /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/services`. Attach `inventory_id` on top of it for lines that move stock, and leave it out for pure fees and charges.

The other identifiers come from elsewhere: `warehouse_id` from `GET /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/warehouses`, `sales_channel_id` from `GET /api/v1/sales-channels`, and `market` as a two-letter marketplace country code such as `US`.

Returns `400` if `transaction_date` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description: Returns a single invoice with every relation resolved: line items with product and service info, customer, warehouse, sales channel, `market` country code, `source` and the linked project task. Responds `404` if the invoice does not belong to the company in `companyUuid`.

put.description:
Updates an invoice. Only fields present in the request body are applied; omitted fields keep their current values. `ref_number` is fixed at creation and cannot be changed — it is ignored if present in the request body. Every other field can be updated.

Only invoices with `source = manual` can be changed — those created in NeonPanel or through this API. Invoices synced from a sales channel (`amazon`, `shopify`, `tiktok`) are read-only and return `400`. Every invoice returns its `source`, so check it before attempting an update rather than relying on the error.

Sending `details` replaces the line items entirely — the existing ones are deleted and re-created — so send the complete set, not only the lines that changed. Each line still requires a `service_id`. The header `amount` is not taken from the request; it is recalculated as the sum of `amount` across the detail lines.

Returns `400` if `transaction_date` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description: Returns the company's shipments, paginated. Each shipment arrives with its line items (including inventory and product info) and its origin and destination warehouses and marketplaces. Date filters are asymmetric: `start_date` applies to `arrived_at` and `end_date` to `shipped_at`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search applied against shipment `ref_number` and `name`.

parameters.name: warehouses
parameters.description: Filter by one or more warehouse IDs (matches origin or destination).

post.description:
Creates a manual shipment. `ref_number` is the only required field. Every other field is optional and nullable, and can be sent here or added later with `PUT`. A project task is created for the document on save, or reused if one already exists.

Returns `400` if `date_shipment_sent` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description: Returns a single shipment with every relation resolved: line items with inventory and product info, origin and destination warehouses and marketplaces, and the linked project task. Responds `404` if the shipment does not belong to the company in `companyUuid`.

put.description:
Updates a shipment. Only fields present in the request body are applied; omitted fields keep their current values. `ref_number` is fixed at creation and cannot be changed — it is ignored if present in the request body. Every other field can be updated.

Only shipments that were entered manually can be changed. If the shipment came from an external document — `document_id` is set — the request returns `400`.

Sending `items` replaces the line items entirely — the existing ones are deleted and re-created — so send the complete set, not only the lines that changed.

Returns `400` if `date_shipment_sent` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description:
Returns the company's services, paginated. Supports free-text search by name. The default page size is 100; override it with `per_page`.

The `id` values returned here are what bill, invoice and adjustment line items reference as `service_id`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search applied against service name.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of results per page. Defaults to 100.

get.description: Returns all sales channels as a flat, non-paginated list. Unlike most resources these are shared across the platform rather than scoped to a company, which is why the path carries no `companyUuid`. Pass `id` as `sales_channel_id` when creating or updating an invoice.

Returns every payment term available to the company as a flat, non-paginated list — both system terms shared across all companies (`system: true`) and terms the company defined itself.

`document` names the document type the term applies to, for example `InventoryOrder` or `Bill`, and is `null` for terms not tied to a type. Pass `id` as `payment_term_id` when creating an inventory order or bill to have payment request installments generated from the term's schema. Changing the term later re-syncs the schedule: installments the new term still needs are kept as they are, the surplus is deleted.

Returns the company's inventory adjustments, paginated. Each adjustment arrives with its line items — which reference either an inventory record for a quantity change or a service for a fee — plus its warehouse, marketplace and linked project task. Supports free-text search and date range filtering by `transaction_date`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search applied across adjustment fields.

post.description:
Creates an inventory adjustment. `ref_number` is the only required field. Every other field is optional and nullable, and can be sent here or added later with `PUT`. A project task is created for the document on save, or reused if one already exists.

Returns `400` if `date` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description: Returns a single adjustment with every relation resolved: line items with product or service info, warehouse, marketplace and the linked project task. Responds `404` if the adjustment does not belong to the company in `companyUuid`.

put.description:
Updates an adjustment. Only fields present in the request body are applied; omitted fields keep their current values. `ref_number` is fixed at creation and cannot be changed — it is ignored if present in the request body. Every other field can be updated.

Sending `details` replaces the line items entirely — the existing ones are deleted and re-created — so send the complete set, not only the lines that changed. The header `amount` is not taken from the request — it is recalculated as the sum of `quantity * rate` across the detail lines.

Returns `400` if `date` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

get.description:
Starts the Authorization Code flow. Send the user's browser here; the server redirects back to the client's `redirect_uri` with either a `code` or an `error`.

Only `response_type=code` is supported. PKCE is supported with `code_challenge_method=S256` and is required for public clients that authenticate with `none`. `redirect_uri` may be omitted when the client registered exactly one, and is required when it registered several. Exchange the returned code at `POST /oauth2/token`.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Optional if a single redirect URI is registered; required if multiple URIs are registered.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque value used to maintain state between the request and callback.

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: PKCE code challenge (required for public clients using PKCE).

Location.description: Redirect target containing the result (`code` or `error`).

post.description:
Issues tokens for the `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, `client_credentials` and `sso_token` grants. The request body is `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

This endpoint authenticates the client, not the user, so it does not take an API access token. Four methods are accepted: `client_secret_basic` (HTTP Basic), `client_secret_post` (credentials in the form body), `private_key_jwt` (RFC 7523, via `client_assertion`), and `none` for public clients using PKCE, subject to server policy.

sso_token.summary: Authorize user without UI using SSO token

post.description:
Registers a new OAuth client under RFC 7591. Registration is open — no Initial Access Token is required.

The response carries a `registration_access_token` and a `registration_client_uri`. Store both: the token is the only credential that can read, update, delete or rotate this client afterwards, and it is valid for 30 days.

get.description: Returns the client's registered metadata. Authenticated with the client's Registration Access Token, not an API access token.

401.description: Missing or invalid registration access token

patch.description: Updates the client's registered metadata and returns the result. Only fields present in the request body are applied. Authenticated with the client's Registration Access Token, not an API access token.

401.description: Missing or invalid registration access token

delete.description: Deletes the registered client. Tokens already issued to it stop being usable. Authenticated with the client's Registration Access Token, not an API access token.

401.description: Missing or invalid registration access token

post.description: Issues a fresh Registration Access Token for the client and revokes the previous one, subject to server policy. The new token is valid for 30 days and is returned only in this response.

401.description: Missing or invalid registration access token or insufficient privileges

post.description: Issues a fresh `client_secret` and revokes the previous one immediately, so deploy the new secret before rotating. The secret is returned only in this response and cannot be retrieved again. `client_secret_expires_at` is currently always `0`, meaning the secret does not expire.

401.description: Missing or invalid registration access token

tags.name: Companies
tags.description: Companies the authenticated user can access. Every company-scoped endpoint takes the `uuid` returned here as its `{companyUuid}` path parameter.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Catalogue of available reports and retrieval of report data.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Aggregated revenue and COGS summaries across companies, marketplaces and periods.

tags.name: Inventory
tags.description: Inventory items: catalogue records, per-item restock data and balances, COGS and landed costs.

tags.name: Warehouses
tags.description: Warehouses belonging to a company, and the inventory balances held in each. Warehouses are referenced by inventory orders, shipments, invoices and adjustments.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Product catalogue. A product groups one or more inventory items.

tags.name: Listings
tags.description: Marketplace listings linked to inventory items, including on-demand sync.

tags.name: Vendors
tags.description: Read-only vendor directory scoped to a company. Supports search and pagination.

tags.name: Services
tags.description: Read-only service directory scoped to a company. Used as line items on Bills, Invoices and Adjustments.

tags.name: Payment Terms
tags.description: Read-only payment terms scoped to a company. Includes both system terms shared across companies (`system: true`) and company-specific terms, each with the document type it applies to.

tags.name: Sales Channels
tags.description: Read-only list of sales channels available across the platform. Referenced by invoice line items.

tags.name: Inventory Orders
tags.description: Purchase orders for inventory. An order references a vendor, a marketplace and a destination warehouse, and carries line items (inventory SKU, quantity, price). An optional payment term generates payment request installments.

tags.name: Bills
tags.description: Vendor bills. Line items reference services looked up (or auto-created) by name. An optional payment term generates payment request installments.

tags.name: Shipments
tags.description: Movements of inventory between warehouses. Only shipments without a linked external document can be modified through the API.

tags.name: Invoices
tags.description: Customer invoices. Every line item carries a service; an inventory SKU can be attached to it for lines that sell stock. Only invoices with `source = manual` can be modified — those synced from Amazon, Shopify or TikTok are read-only.

tags.name: Assembly Orders
tags.description: Assembly (kitting) orders. Create and update are rejected when `date_order_assembled` is earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date.

tags.name: Adjustments
tags.description: Inventory adjustments. Line items either change the quantity of an inventory SKU or record a service fee. Supports free-text search and `transaction_date` range filtering.

tags.name: Payment Requests
tags.description: Payment installments generated from documents (Inventory Orders, Bills). Each installment is returned with its parent document context and can be filtered by `due_date`.

tags.name: Import
tags.description: Document import: format instructions, structured (JSON) creation, PDF upload and processing status.

tags.name: OAuth2
tags.description: OAuth 2.0 authorization and token endpoints (RFC 6749) with PKCE S256.

tags.name: Client Registration
tags.description: Dynamic Client Registration and client lifecycle management (RFC 7591 / RFC 7592).

OAuth2.description: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE (S256). Send the resulting access token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Refresh with `grant_type=refresh_token` on the token endpoint.

scopes.openid: Access the API on behalf of the authenticated user.

ClientSecretBasic.description: Token-endpoint client authentication: HTTP Basic with `client_id` / `client_secret`.

ClientSecretPost.name: X-Client-Auth-Form
ClientSecretPost.description: Token-endpoint client authentication: `client_id` and `client_secret` sent as form fields in the request body. Declared as a header scheme only because OpenAPI cannot express body-based client authentication.

PrivateKeyJWT.description: Token-endpoint client authentication with `private_key_jwt` (RFC 7523). Send `client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer` and `client_assertion=<JWT signed with the client's private key>`.

RegistrationAccessToken.description: Registration Access Token (RAT) issued by `POST /oauth2/register`. Required for reading, updating, deleting and rotating a client. Valid for 30 days; this is **not** an API access token.

details.description: Line items for the adjustment. If provided, all existing lines are deleted and replaced with this array.

reason.description: Reason for the adjustment. Currently one of `Damaged`, `Misplaced`, `Administrative Errors`; additional values may be added over time.

payment_term.description: Payment term attached to this bill, if any.

client_secret.description: Returned when the chosen auth method issues a secret.

DocumentResource.description: Contextual reference to the parent document that owns this payment request. Returns an empty object if the document relation is null. The `type` field is the short class name of the underlying model (e.g. `InventoryOrder`, `Bill`, `Shipment`). `ref_number` and `date` are present for all supported document types: `FifoDocument` implementors (includes `InventoryOrder` and others), `Bill`, and `ShipmentExtension`. Project-related fields (`link`, `status`, `completed`) are only present when the document has an associated project.

id.description: Primary key of the underlying document model.

type.description: Short class name of the underlying document model.

link.description: URL to the project task view in the processes UI.

status.description: Name of the kanban column the project is currently in.

completed.description: Datetime when the project was marked as completed.

ref_number.description: Document reference number (present for FifoDocument / ShipmentExtension models only).

date.description: FIFO transaction date of the document, field name resolved dynamically via `getFifoTransactionDateAttribute()` (present for FifoDocument / ShipmentExtension models only).

ErrorResource.description: Standard error envelope used across the API.

ImportType.description: Lowercase import type. Currently only **bill** is supported.

InventoryOrderPayload.description: Fields accepted when creating or updating an inventory order. All fields are optional on update (sparse patch). On create, `ref_number` is used as the human-readable PO reference stored in `order_id`.

name.description: Free-text display name for the order.

ref_number.description: Human-readable reference / PO number. Used only during create (`sometimes` rule); ignored on update.

date_manufacturing_completed.description: Date manufacturing was completed / goods were received (maps to `date_order_received`).

market.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the marketplace, for example `US`. Must match the code of a marketplace the platform knows; the server resolves it to the marketplace internally.

warehouse_id.description: FK to the inventory_warehouses table (destination warehouse).

payment_term_id.description: FK to the payment_terms table. When set, the server calls `PaymentRequestService::handlePaymentTermsSchema` to auto-generate installment records for this order.

InventoryOrderResource.description: Full representation of an inventory order as returned by the API.

link.description: URL to the project task view. Null if no project exists.

ref_number.description: Human-readable PO reference (stored as `order_id` on the model).

total_amount.description: Sum of (quantity × price) across all line items. Computed server-side when `details` is provided.

payment_term.description: Payment term attached to this order, if any.

inventory_id.description: ID of the inventory record being sold. Omit it or pass null for service-only lines such as fees and charges.

service_id.description: ID of the associated service, from `GET /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/services`. Required on every line.

quantity.description: Quantity as displayed: positive sells stock, negative returns it. Stored as sent; the underlying inventory transaction uses the opposite sign.

amount.description: Total monetary amount for this line, taken as given rather than derived from a rate. The invoice header `amount` is recalculated as the sum of these values.

InvoiceDetailPayload.description: A single invoice line item. `service_id` is required on every line, including lines that sell stock. Add `inventory_id` when the line moves inventory; omit it for pure fees and charges.

InvoiceDetailResource.description: A single invoice line item. Every line references a service; `inventory_id`, `sku` and `product_name` are populated only on lines that also move stock.

sku.description: Product SKU from the linked inventory record.

quantity.description: Quantity as displayed: positive means stock was sold, negative means it came back, for example on a customer return. The sign is inverted relative to the underlying inventory transaction.

InvoiceListResponse.description: Paginated wrapper returned by the invoices list endpoint.

filters.description: Echo of the filter params that were applied.

InvoicePayload.description:
Fields accepted when creating or updating a manual invoice. `ref_number` is required on create and ignored on update; every other field is optional and nullable in both.

If `details` is provided, existing line items are replaced entirely and the header `amount` is recalculated as the sum of `amount` across the detail lines.

Field names match the response throughout: `sales_channel_id` comes back as the `sales_channel` object carrying the same `id`, and `market` comes back as the same country code.

name.description: Free-text display name for the invoice.

ref_number.description: Human-readable reference number. Required on create; ignored on update, so an invoice reference cannot be changed once issued.

transaction_date.description: Transaction date (ISO 8601). Must not be earlier than the company's Entry Locked Date; otherwise the request returns `400`.

market.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the marketplace, for example `US`. Must match the code of a marketplace the platform knows. Returned unchanged as `market` — invoices work with the code in both directions, never with a numeric marketplace ID.

warehouse_id.description: ID of the warehouse associated with this invoice, from `GET /api/v1/companies/{companyUuid}/warehouses`.

customer_id.description: ID of the customer this invoice is issued to. The API does not expose a customer directory yet, so for now this ID has to come from an invoice you have already read back.

sales_channel_id.description: ID of the sales channel the sale was made through, from `GET /api/v1/sales-channels`. Returned as the `sales_channel` object, whose `id` is this same value.

details.description: Line items for the invoice. If provided, all existing lines are deleted and replaced with this array, so send the complete set.

InvoiceResource.description: Full representation of an invoice as returned by the API.

link.description: URL to the project task view. Null if no project exists.

source.description: How the invoice entered NeonPanel. `manual` covers invoices created in the application or through this API and is the only source that can be edited; the others are synced from the named sales channel and are read-only.

transaction_date.description: Transaction date (ISO 8601). Accepted under the same name on create and update.

market.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the marketplace this sale belongs to, for example `US`. The same code is what the write side accepts as `market`.

amount.description: Total invoice amount, recalculated from the line items rather than set directly.

sales_channel.description: Sales channel the sale was made through, or `null` when none is assigned. Its `id` is the same value the write side takes as `sales_channel_id`, so an invoice read from the API can be sent back without a lookup.

bullet_points.description:
Bullet points grouped by language tag.
Each key is a BCP 47 language tag (e.g. en_US, de_DE), and
the value is an ordered list of bullet point strings.

PaymentRequestListResponse.description: Paginated wrapper returned by the payment requests list endpoint.

filters.description: Echo of the filter params that were applied.

amount_due.description: Total amount due for this installment (set by the payment term schema).

due_date.description: Deadline for this installment (set by the payment term schema).

classification.description: Internal classification tag for accounting purposes.

system.description: True if this is a system term shared across all companies; false if it belongs to the requested company.

document.description: Short class name of the document type this term applies to, resolved via reflection from the stored FQCN (e.g. `InventoryOrder`, `Bill`). Null if the term is universal — applicable to all document types.

schema.description: Ordered list of installment definitions parsed from the stored schema string. Each entry defines what percentage of the total is due, anchored to a document date field plus an optional day offset.

PaymentTermSchemaItem.description: A single installment entry within a payment term schema.

date_anchor.description: Name of the document date field used as the anchor for this installment's due date (e.g. `date_order_placed` for Inventory Orders, `date` for Bills).

days_offset.description: Number of days added to the `date_anchor` value to calculate the installment due date. Zero means due on the anchor date itself.

percentage.description: Percentage of the document total due for this installment.

link.description: Base URL to open the report. To open a specific sheet with filters, append query parameters to this URL (see sheets[].slug and sheets[].parameters[].slug).

sheets.description:
List of available report sheets. Each sheet defines which query parameters can be used.
Build the report URL by appending query parameters to `link`: {link}?sheet={sheets[].slug}&{paramSlug}={value}&...
The `sheet` query parameter is optional. If `sheet` is not provided, the report will open the first available sheet by default.
You can additionally pass the `company` query parameter as a comma-separated list of company IDs. Each value is the numeric `id` returned by `GET /api/v1/companies` — not `uuid` and not `short_name`. The order of query parameters does not matter.
Example: https://my.neonpanel.com/app/reports/basic_suite_new/v3-inventory-transactions-bas-user?company=106,296&sheet=transaction-list&start-date=2026-02-01&end-date=2026-02-13

slug.description: Sheet identifier. Use this value as the `sheet` query parameter when building the report URL. Example: {link}?sheet={slug}

parameters.description: Filters/parameters supported by this sheet. Each item describes one query parameter. Use parameter.slug as the query parameter name.

slug.description: A slug name that can be used in Report link alongside sheet

type.description: UI control type. It also implies how to format the value in the URL: - DateTimePicker: use `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. 2026-02-01) or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` - DateTimeRangePicker: usually represented by two params (e.g. start-date/end-date) if present in parameters list - Dropdown + multiselect=true: value is comma-separated list

multiselect.description:
Applies to Dropdown only. - If type=Dropdown and multiselect=true: pass selected values as a single comma-separated string.
  Example: brand=Nike,Adidas
- Otherwise: pass a single value.

count.description: Count of Reports available and accessible

company.description: Company data if in grouping parameter company was provided

country_code.description: Country code if in grouping parameter country was provided

invoice.description: Invoice data if in grouping parameter invoice was provided

issued_at.description: Issuance time as seconds since epoch.
